title: remote customer cluster (win-claas)
summary: A customer-side cluster of the CLAAS line: a remote enterprise host reached over SSH, installed by the same Gradle pipeline as every other target. Surveyed against the server project 2026-07-28 -- no field below is guessed. Two things this does NOT claim: nobody has connected to that cluster from this console, and what the console is permitted to do there is an operator decision no repository can answer (see CONSOLE_PERMITTED).

fields.comment: the remote enterprise host. The server project reads the same value as REMOTE_DEPLOY_HOST out of its own gitignored config/dot_env/.env (vpath_server lib/vm.sh:412) -- declare it here, never copy the .env
SSH, key-based, no passwords. The pipeline routes every kubectl call through it (vpath_server lib/vm.sh:503-505, .claude/skills/reinstall/SKILL.md:411)

fields.example: <none in the server project -- set only if your network adds one>
fields.comment: no bastion is configured: the server project connects to the host directly (vpath_server lib/vm.sh:503-505). Declare one only if the customer network actually requires it

fields.example: operator's default SSH keypair, public key in the host's authorized_keys
fields.comment: key-based, no passwords; unlike the NUC path the callsite passes no -i, so the operator's ssh default/ssh_config decides the key (vpath_server lib/vm.sh:503 vs 639-643, SKILL.md:33-37). Structure only -- the key itself is never declared here

fields.example: same Gradle pipeline; build VM local to the operator, deploy over SSH
fields.comment: the SAME pipeline as every other target, identical from provisionBuildVM onward -- only VM lifecycle differs (vpath_server README.md:18, SKILL.md 'Windows Variant')

fields.example: <OPEN -- state what this console may do on the customer system>
fields.comment: the one open question, and deliberately left open: the server project documents no approval path, change window or customer consent anywhere, because this is an operator and customer decision, not a code fact. Until it is answered the console drives nothing here -- the transport refuses this kind outright

fields.example: <customer site> / <filesystem root on the deploy host>
fields.comment: location question 1 -- a remote enterprise host at the customer, not a machine we own (vpath_server README.md:16)

fields.example: on the operator's own machine (QEMU build VM), not on the customer host
fields.comment: location question 2 -- DIFFERS from a NUC. A NUC is build host and deploy host in one (vpath_server lib/vm.sh:387-392); here the build VM is local to the operator and only the deploy host is remote (SKILL.md:29-34)
location question 3 -- the same sources as any other target, since it is the same pipeline (vpath_server README.md:18)

fields.default: in-cluster registry on the deploy host, filled by skopeo
fields.comment: location question 4 -- DIFFERS from a NUC. Images are built where there is internet and written in with `skopeo copy docker-daemon: docker://`; the host itself must never reach the internet, which the verifyAirgap phase gate enforces (vpath_server README.md:18, analysis/app-ify/08-airgap-packaging.md:123-124)
